claim: Hepatic sarcopenia is associated with high mortality in liver cirrhosis.

claim: Increased bile acids are altered in hepatic sarcopenia.

claim: LCA can regulate muscle mass via a liver-muscle axis.
source: These results from CLD rats and human subjects suggest that LCA can regulate muscle mass via a liver-muscle axis
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined rat and human data.

claim: A decrease in serum LCA level portends a worse survival outcome in CLD patients with associated low muscle mass.
source: Furthermore, we revealed that a decrease in serum LCA level portends a worse survival outcome in CLD patients with associated low muscle mass.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the survival analysis data.

claim: CLD patients with sarcopenia, defined by low muscle mass and power, display decreased survival when compared to CLD patients without sarcopenia.
source: CLD patients with sarcopenia, defined by low muscle mass and power, also display decreased survival when compared to CLD patients without sarcopenia (Hara et al., 2016)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Serum LCA may be a useful measure to monitor sarcopenia in CLD patients.
source: thus serum LCA may be a useful measure to monitor sarcopenia in CLD patients.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the association between LCA levels and muscle mass/survival.

claim: LCA is one of the most potent anti-bacterial agents, selective against gram-positive bacteria, resulting in a longer lifespan of centenarians.
source: Current reports have also demonstrated that LCA is one of the most potent anti-bacterial agents, selective against gram-positive bacteria, resulting in a longer lifespan of centenarians (Sato et al., 2021)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: LCA is one of the most potent endogenous ligands for TGR5, which protects against alcohol-induced liver steatosis and inflammation in mice.
source: and is one of the most potent endogenous ligands for TGR5, which protects against alcohol-induced liver steatosis and inflammation in mice (Iracheta-Vellve et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: LCA plays a critical role in the progression of CLD and intestinal microbiota as a function of the liver-gut axis.
source: This evidence clearly shows that LCA plays a critical role in the progression of CLD and intestinal microbiota as a function of the liver-gut axis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from cited evidence about LCA's multiple roles.

claim: The association of LCA with skeletal muscle mass will lead to new insights into the role of LCA as a component of the liver-muscle-gut axis.
source: Our latest results presented here, associating LCA with skeletal muscle mass, will lead to new insights into the role of LCA as a component of the liver-muscle-gut axis.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the implications of the findings.

claim: In CLD rats and human subjects, an association between gastrocnemius muscle mass and LCA only was observed, although serum CA, CDCA, and DCA levels also showed a decreasing trend in CLD patients with low muscle mass.
source: In CLD rats and human subjects, we observed an association between gastrocnemius muscle mass and LCA only, although serum CA, CDCA, and DCA levels also showed a decreasing trend in CLD patients with low muscle mass.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the observed associations.

claim: The hierarchy of BA affinity for TGR5 is as follows: LCA>DCA> CDCA>CA.
source: This result is reasonable since the hierarchy of BA affinity for TGR5 is as follows: LCA>DCA> CDCA>CA (Sato et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: A TGR5 antagonist induced skeletal muscle cell hypertrophy through IGF-1 activation.
source: We also demonstrated that a TGR5 antagonist induced skeletal muscle cell hypertrophy through IGF-1 activation
evidence: This appears to be an error in the manuscript - the text likely means 'agonist' not 'antagonist' based on the experimental results. This is supported by the cell culture experiments.

claim: LCA has new roles as a positive regulator of skeletal muscle mass in both CLD rats and human patients.
source: In conclusion, we revealed new roles for LCA as a positive regulator of skeletal muscle mass in both CLD rats and human patients
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: LCA is a mediator of skeletal muscle cell hypertrophy in differentiated C2C12 myoblasts (myotubes).
source: In conclusion, we revealed new roles for LCA as a positive regulator of skeletal muscle mass in both CLD rats and human patients and as a mediator of skeletal muscle cell hypertrophy in differentiated C2C12 myoblasts (myotubes).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cell culture experiments.

claim: The serum LCA ratio measurement was significantly decreased in CLD patients with low muscle mass.
source: The serum LCA ratio measurement was significantly decreased in CLD patients with low muscle mass.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the patient data analysis.

claim: Serum LCA levels may be used as a prognostic factor of survival in CLD patients with sarcopenia.
source: Current results suggest that serum LCA levels may be used as a prognostic factor of survival in CLD patients with sarcopenia
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the survival analysis data with speculative implications.

claim: A TGR5 agonist holds the potential to be a candidate as a therapeutic target in the prevention of sarcopenia in CLD patients.
source: and a TGR5 agonist holds the potential to be a candidate as a therapeutic target in the prevention of sarcopenia in CLD patients.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications based on the experimental findings.
